info.title: MonsoonQuant API
info.description: Research analytics for India's exchange-traded rainfall futures. Not investment advice.

get.description:
SPEC's "all 4 methods side-by-side" — currently returns whichever
methods/measures actually have real rows written for this series
(burn and dist, per M4; conditioned/mpr rungs not yet written to
this table — see docs/STATUS.md), not a fabricated 4-method set.

Each method's own MOST RECENT row, not "whatever was written on the
literal same calendar day" — real data showed burn and dist were
written a day apart for RAINCHNNAI (M4 ran them in separate passes),
so a same-day join would have silently dropped one method entirely
whenever `as_of` isn't given. `as_of`, when given, bounds every
method's own latest row to "at or before that date" rather than
requiring an exact match.

The real M3 `index_values` rows: proxy (satellite/model-derived)
vs. official index value per observed day, plus the proxy's own
error against the official value where both exist.

`index_values` is keyed (series_id, obs_date, as_of_date) because a
given obs_date's proxy estimate can be revised as more data arrives
-- same "each day's own most recent snapshot" rule as
`valuations/compare` above, bounded by `as_of` when given rather than
requiring an exact match.

Real `market_quotes` rows (SPEC §9.2: "settle, volume, OI"). Will
legitimately return an empty list for both real series right now --
NCDEX's bhavcopy live fetch stays bot-gated (M2, documented policy),
so no real settlement data has ever been ingested; this is reported
honestly as zero rows, not backfilled with synthetic quotes.

Real `mpr_estimates` rows (SPEC §9.2: "lambda time series + CIs +
liquidity"), M6's Wang/Esscher calibration output. Will legitimately
return an empty list right now: M6's demo ran against illustrative
settle data only (no real NCDEX settlement exists yet, same bhavcopy
bot-gate as `quotes` above), so nothing has been written to this
table against real market data -- reported honestly, not faked.

Quantiles + fan-chart data (SPEC §9.2) straight from the real,
hash-chained `prediction_ledger` (M7's backtest rows) -- the same
source `/v1/ledger` reads, just scoped to one series and shaped for
a fan chart (one quantile set per as_of_date) instead of raw ledger
rows. The ledger is keyed by `contract_code`, not `series_id` (a
forecast target like "remaining season rainfall" applies to the
whole contract, not one listed expiry), so `series_id` is resolved
to its `contract_code` via the real `contracts` table first.

SPEC §10 page 3's "analog-years table" -- which real historical
seasons `analog_v1` actually used, for a live `as_of` (defaults to
today). Not stored anywhere (the ledger row only carries the
resulting quantiles, SPEC's own stated gap -- M7), so this is a
real, on-demand re-run of just the analog-selection step
(`mq.forecasting.live.get_live_analog_forecast`), not the full
4-rung live-forecast build `mq ledger write-live` does.

GeoJSON grid metrics (SPEC §9.2) -- a real, on-demand run of M10's
basis-risk engine for this series' own contract spec (there's no
`basis_results` table; the real M10 run, `docs/methods/basis.md`,
covered 12 real IMD grid cells for RAINCHNNAI's ~1 deg box). Cached
by request hash (series_id, as_of, box_deg) after a real, measured
~48s uncached run -- see `_basis_cache` above for why.

`box_deg` controls the half-width of the bounding box (degrees)
around the contract's own station(s), default 0.5 deg to match the
real M10 run; the real IMD grid's own 0.25 deg native spacing means
this box typically yields a handful to a few dozen cells, not an
unbounded scan.

post.description:
Real M9 hedge optimisation: min-variance AND CVaR95 positions for
a candidate exposure location, against the real contract index.
Cached by request hash (SPEC §9.3).

**No position constraints by default -- and that can matter a lot
for `cvar95`.** `docs/methods/hedge.md` documents a real finding:
the real RAINCHNNAI index has been positive in all 31 historical
seasons, so an *unconstrained* CVaR95 minimization has no interior
optimum and genuinely wants to short without limit -- confirmed live
via this endpoint itself (an unconstrained request lands at
`LotConstraints`' own 10,000-lot fallback cap with an extreme CVaR
figure). This is the real, correct LP answer to an unconstrained
question, not sanitized or capped by the API -- pass `constraints`
(e.g. `max_order_lots`, `margin_budget`) for a realistic position.

Real M11 parametric-cover optimisation (SPEC §9.2): grid search +
Nelder-Mead refine over `(trigger, slope, limit)` to minimize
basis-failure probability subject to a premium budget, against a
real candidate location's real loss sample and the real official
index -- `mq.risk.parametric.optimize_cover` directly, no new
pricing math. Cached by request hash (SPEC §9.3).

Exposure is the same illustrative-on-real-data pattern as `/v1/hedge`
(SPEC's own §7.11 posture): a real location's real CDR reconstruction
run through one of SPEC's named exposure templates. The real M11 run
(`docs/methods/parametric.md`) found an unrestricted trigger grid lets
the optimizer find a degenerate near-always-pay cover -- the default
`trigger_grid` here (median-to-max of the real index) avoids that by
the same restriction the real run used; passing a grid that starts
below the median reproduces the degenerate case, deliberately not
guarded against here since it's a legitimate optimum of the literal
objective, not an error.

Real M11 scenario lab: each named shock (ENSO/IOD presets, a
cloudburst bump, or a real historical-year ONI/DMI analog) re-runs
the real simulator + Greeks under the shocked covariates, against a
real fitted chain model. Cached by request hash (SPEC §9.3);
`n_paths` capped at 200k per SPEC.

get.description:
Real M9 Greeks: delta/gamma via common random numbers (exact CRN
pairing -- structurally delta=1.0/gamma=0 for this CDR index, see
`docs/methods/greeks.md`), theta via the two partial-pairing bump
scenarios (no-rain-day / climatological-day), each reporting its own
standard error and SE-as-fraction-of-value per SPEC's SE<5% bar.
theta is omitted (not computed) when `start_date >= period_end`,
since there's no remaining season to bump a day into.

`n_paths` capped at 200k per SPEC; higher `n_paths` is what actually
lets theta meet the SE<5% bar in practice (`docs/methods/greeks.md`'s
real run needed ~1,000,000 paths via the C++ core at n_paths that
large -- this route still uses the NumPy-level `mq.risk.greeks`
functions, so very large `n_paths` here will be proportionally
slower; no request-hash cache yet, unlike the POSTs, since repeated
identical GETs are a smaller concern than this endpoint's real
per-call cost).

Real M7 walk-forward backtest, all 5 ladder rungs (clim_baseline,
enso_clim_v1, analog_v1, lgbm_q_v1, lgbm_q_cqr_v1), against real IMD
rainfall + real ONI/DMI. CRPSS is reported honestly -- M7's own real
run found every newer rung underperforms climatology at n=31 seasons
(`docs/methods/forecasting.md`), and this live re-run is expected to
reproduce that, not a nicer-looking number. Cached by
(contract_code, as_of).

get.description:
Full real data/model lineage for one series: the contract spec's
own version + real source document IDs, every real `valuations` row
with its (currently always-null, see module docstring) `run_id`,
the latest real `index_values` snapshot's `data_version`, and every
real `prediction_ledger` row for the series' own contract (richer
lineage: model_id/model_version/data_version/hashes). `as_of`, when
given, bounds every source to "at or before that date".

multiplier.title: Multiplier
multiplier.description: INR per index point; defaults to the contract's own spec value

loss_threshold.title: Loss Threshold
loss_threshold.description: Defaults to the P75 (worst-quartile) of the real loss sample

trigger_grid.title: Trigger Grid
trigger_grid.description: Defaults to 8 points from the real index's own median to its max -- SPEC's real finding (docs/methods/parametric.md): an unrestricted grid starting at the index's minimum lets the optimizer find a degenerate near-always-pay cover

historical_analog_years.title: Historical Analog Years
historical_analog_years.description: Real ONI/DMI from these real historical years (e.g. 2015 for SPEC's Chennai-floods analog), from the real ingested climate_idx data

observed_to_date.title: Observed To Date
observed_to_date.description: CDR spot already accumulated before start_date; defaults to the latest real index_values row for this series
